main.title: Dead Space 2
main.subtitle: Isaac returns aboard the Sprawl
main.summary: Dead Space 2 is a 2011 survival horror game developed by Visceral Games and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: Isaac returns aboard the Sprawl
cards.text: Dead Space 2 is a 2011 survival horror game developed by Visceral Games and published by Electronic Arts. It was released for PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360 in January. The second mainline entry in the Dead Space series, set on the Titan-based Sprawl space station, follows series protagonist Isaac Clarke as he fights against both an outbreak of the monstrous Necromorphs and debilitating mental illness induced by the alien Markers. Gameplay features Isaac exploring a series of levels, solving puzzles to progress, and finding resources while fighting off Necromorphs. The game included a competitive multiplayer, with the Sprawl's security forces fighting teams of Necromorphs.

cards.heading: The suit becomes the interface
cards.text: Isaac's RIG shows health and energy on his back, while weapons display ammunition. Holographic menus leave the action running as the player checks inventory or logs. Kinesis moves objects and can launch severed limbs at enemies; Stasis slows a target briefly. Jet packs allow movement through zero gravity, and vacuum sections limit Isaac to his remaining air supply. Timed hacking puzzles open some doors and devices.

cards.heading: Feedback changes combat and exploration
cards.text: Gameplay elements were included based on positive feedback from the first game. The main additions were destructible environments, included to offer gameplay variety and increase the realism, and launching objects at enemies, which allowed for players to fight when out of ammunition. The team wanted each level to feel unique for players, with Papoutis citing the level in a Unitologist Church as an example of "[keeping] players on their toes". The Ishimura level had little to no enemy encounters to reinforce the tension and the game's themes, with art director Ian Milham successfully pushing back against requests to add in more enemy encounters. Some of the puzzle and level designs were toned down for the final release after negative tester feedback about their difficulty. An early suggested concept was having Isaac voice suggestions if players were struggling with a puzzle. The diegetic UI design was carried over from the original game, with some elements during the opening section tying into the portrayal of Isaac's mental state.

main.title: The Last Story
main.subtitle: A mercenary’s ambition
main.summary: The Last Story is a Wii role-playing game directed by Hironobu Sakaguchi, with music by Nobuo Uematsu. Zael belongs to a band of mercenaries and dreams of becoming a knight. Work brings the group to Lazulis Island, where personal ambitions become entangled with power, conflict and a world in decline. His relationship with Calista provides a central thread through the adventure. The game gives this fantasy story a more immediate physical setting through real-time battles and the presence of companions around its protagonist.

cards.heading: A mercenary’s ambition
cards.text: The Last Story is a Wii role-playing game directed by Hironobu Sakaguchi, with music by Nobuo Uematsu. Zael belongs to a band of mercenaries and dreams of becoming a knight. Work brings the group to Lazulis Island, where personal ambitions become entangled with power, conflict and a world in decline. His relationship with Calista provides a central thread through the adventure. The game gives this fantasy story a more immediate physical setting through real-time battles and the presence of companions around its protagonist.

cards.heading: Drawing the enemy’s attention
cards.text: Zael’s Gathering ability makes nearby enemies focus on him, buying time for his companions to act without interruption. That turns drawing danger into a useful role within the party. Commands allow the player to direct allies, while spells leave elemental circles on the ground. Walking through one can give a weapon its element; later, Zael can diffuse a circle to spread its effect. Positioning therefore matters for more than avoiding an attack: it determines who is protected and how the group can use its magic.

cards.heading: Cover and a clear shot
cards.text: Zael can take cover behind objects, breaking an enemy’s line of sight, and use a crossbow from an over-the-shoulder view. Aiming at an opponent reveals information about its abilities and weaknesses. Destructible parts of the scenery offer further ways to influence a fight. Between missions, Lazulis City provides shops, side quests and an arena where the party can improve and earn rewards. These different activities give the mercenaries practical work to do around the island, beyond following the central story.

main.title: Valkyria Chronicles III
main.subtitle: The war follows soldiers without names
main.summary: Valkyria Chronicles III is Sega and Media.Vision's PSP tactical role-playing game, released in Japan on 27 January 2011. Its story runs alongside the original Valkyria Chronicles, following the Nameless, a penal military unit assigned dangerous operations during Gallia's war. The viewpoint changes the campaign's meaning: the player commands soldiers whose place within the army is already precarious. The series' combination of tactical planning and directly controlled movement remains, but the story concentrates on a smaller group fighting through work that others prefer to leave unacknowledged. Familiar history becomes another set of personal circumstances.

cards.heading: The war follows soldiers without names
cards.text: Valkyria Chronicles III is Sega and Media.Vision's PSP tactical role-playing game, released in Japan on 27 January 2011. Its story runs alongside the original Valkyria Chronicles, following the Nameless, a penal military unit assigned dangerous operations during Gallia's war. The viewpoint changes the campaign's meaning: the player commands soldiers whose place within the army is already precarious. The series' combination of tactical planning and directly controlled movement remains, but the story concentrates on a smaller group fighting through work that others prefer to leave unacknowledged. Familiar history becomes another set of personal circumstances.

cards.heading: Give each soldier a place in the operation
cards.text: The player distributes actions across the unit, then controls a selected soldier while moving, taking cover and attacking. Decisions made from the tactical view are tested by the route actually taken through enemy fire. The group must be developed across the campaign, making its abilities part of planning for the next assignment. The format carries forward work from Valkyria Chronicles II while adjusting the systems for this different cast. The player has to connect a larger operational plan to the limited distance and immediate dangers one soldier can manage at a time.

cards.heading: A Japanese release with an international following
cards.text: Takeshi Ozawa returned as director, with Raita Honjou providing character designs and Hitoshi Sakimoto composing the music. The opening theme was performed by May'n. An expanded edition followed in November 2011, but the game was not officially localised after the preceding PSP title's limited sales. A fan translation for that expanded release appeared in 2014. Valkyria Chronicles III remains a distinctive parallel story within the series, using the same broad war to ask what it looks like from a unit whose members have been stripped of their ordinary military identities.

main.title: Marvel vs. Capcom 3: Fate of Two Worlds
main.subtitle: Three on Three Between Comics and Arcades
main.summary: Three-character teams turn Marvel and Capcom fighters into combinations of active attacks, assists and timed resources.

cards.heading: Build a team of three
cards.text: Marvel vs. Capcom 3: Fate of Two Worlds brought its crossover to PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in 2011. A team contains three fighters drawn from Marvel comics and Capcom games. The selection makes unlikely combinations possible before a round begins: recognisable characters become parts of a team the player has assembled.

cards.heading: The fighter waiting offscreen
cards.text: Calling an assist brings a teammate briefly into the fight. That extra attack can cover an approach or extend a combination, while changing the active fighter changes the available moves. Learning a team involves the relationships between its members, not only the commands of a favourite character.

cards.heading: A last chance with X-Factor
cards.text: X-Factor offers a limited burst of enhanced ability, giving a struggling team a way to turn the match. It adds a decision about when to spend a powerful resource. The spectacle of beams and airborne combinations rests on these choices about order, support and timing.

main.title: Killzone 3
main.subtitle: An invasion turns into a struggle to leave Helghan alive
main.summary: Killzone 3 continues Sev and Rico's campaign after the fall of Helghan's dictator. Their surviving ISA forces are short of supplies, while rival Helghast leaders compete for control. Released in North America on 22 February 2011, Guerrilla Games' PlayStation 3 shooter carries the retreat through frozen installations, alien vegetation and the wreckage left by the previous battle.

cards.heading: Surviving the aftermath
cards.text: Killzone 3 continues Sev and Rico's campaign after the fall of Helghan's dictator. Their surviving ISA forces are short of supplies, while rival Helghast leaders compete for control. Released in North America on 22 February 2011, Guerrilla Games' PlayStation 3 shooter carries the retreat through frozen installations, alien vegetation and the wreckage left by the previous battle.

cards.heading: A jump into the fight
cards.text: The jetpack changes how a position can be approached. A burst lifts the player into the air, and forward thrust extends the jump before another landing is needed. A wall or gap can become a route toward higher ground, but the movement still requires somewhere safe to come down. Encounters with flying enemies give this extra mobility an opponent to answer, moving some of the fight above the lines of cover on the ground.

cards.heading: New ground and new controls
cards.text: Weapons and vehicles break up the advance through Helghan's different environments. The WASP launcher offers guided fire, while mounted guns place the player inside larger moving battles. Close encounters have their own forceful melee attacks. The original release also supported stereoscopic 3D displays and PlayStation Move aiming, including Sony's Sharp Shooter accessory. These options were built around the same campaign, allowing different ways to view and aim within its combat spaces.

cards.heading: Two soldiers on one screen
cards.text: A split-screen campaign lets a second player share the attempt to survive. The partners must stay aware of each other's position while moving between cover and selecting targets. Online multiplayer continued the class and objective-based structure, with abilities that could support an ally or control part of a route. Both forms place an individual shot inside a larger task: reaching the next position together or giving the rest of the team a useful opening.

main.title: Bulletstorm
main.subtitle: A shooter built around skill points
main.summary: Bulletstorm is a 2011 first-person shooter game developed by People Can Fly and Epic Games and published by Electronic Arts (EA).

cards.heading: A shooter built around skill points
cards.text: Bulletstorm is a 2011 first-person shooter game developed by People Can Fly and Epic Games and published by Electronic Arts (EA). The video game is distinguished by its system of rewarding players with "skillpoints" for performing increasingly creative kills. Bulletstorm does not have any competitive multiplayer modes, preferring instead to include cooperative online play and score attack modes. Set in the 26th century, the game's story follows Grayson Hunt, a space pirate and former black ops soldier who gets shot down on a war-torn planet while trying to exact revenge on General Sarrano, his former commander who tricked him and his men into committing war crimes and assassinating innocents.

cards.heading: Weapons invite unusual combinations
cards.text: As a first-person shooter, Bulletstorm focuses on combat. The game features eight weapons, each with their own distinct behaviors. In addition to standard firearms such as shotguns and assault rifles, the game features unusual weaponry such as the "Bouncer", which shoots explosive bouncing cannonballs, and the "Flailgun", a cannon that shoots bolas weighted by grenades. Each weapon has an alternate fire mode that uses "charges"; for example, the Screamer revolver's "charge shot" turns the weapon into a flare gun that ignites an enemy and sends them into the air.

cards.heading: The leash connects movement, enemies and scenery
cards.text: Grayson's leash pulls an enemy into reach, while kicks and slides send them towards hazards or into the air. Suspended targets move slowly enough for a planned follow-up. The game rewards these combinations as skillshots: an airborne kill, an impact with spikes or a weapon's unusual function can earn more than a straightforward shot. Those points buy ammunition, weapons and upgrades at dropkits. Fighting creatively therefore feeds the tools available for the next encounter, making the surroundings part of the attack rather than scenery beyond it.

main.title: Nintendo 3DS
main.subtitle: Depth without glasses
main.summary: Nintendo 3DS combined a glasses-free stereoscopic display with familiar dual screens, new controls and connections that continued while the lid was closed.

cards.heading: Depth without glasses
cards.text: Nintendo 3DS retained a recognisable arrangement: two screens, physical buttons and a touchscreen below. Its upper display changed what that familiar object could show. Stereoscopic depth was visible without wearing special glasses, and a slider let players adjust the effect or turn it off. The first systems arrived in Japan on 26 February 2011.

cards.heading: New controls, an older library
cards.text: A Circle Pad added analogue movement beside the D-pad. Cameras, motion sensing and a gyroscope gave software further ways to respond to the world around the screen. Older DS and DSi game cards remained usable, so the new machine carried an existing library into a different set of possibilities. Not every game had to use every feature; choosing which inputs mattered remained a design decision.

cards.heading: A special edition in the first year
cards.text: The hardware's identity also appeared through later colours and special editions. Nintendo's black-and-gold Zelda 25th Anniversary bundle reached Europe on 25 November 2011, with a Hyrule emblem and Ocarina of Time 3D. It used the same first-year 3DS body. The larger XL and later New Nintendo 3DS designs were separate revisions.

cards.heading: A closed lid can still do something
cards.text: StreetPass exchanged data with nearby 3DS systems in sleep mode; SpotPass could receive material through supported wireless connections. Nintendo also included cameras for stereoscopic photographs and cards for augmented-reality play. The hardware proposed activities between game sessions, not only more elaborate pictures during them.

main.title: Professor Layton and the Miracle Mask
main.subtitle: A gentleman behind a mask
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Miracle Mask is Level-5's puzzle adventure set in Monte d'Or, a city troubled by the apparently supernatural performances of a masked gentleman. Hershel Layton arrives with Luke and Emmy after receiving a request from an old friend. The investigation also returns to his youth, connecting the present mystery with an earlier expedition. Released alongside the Nintendo 3DS in Japan, it introduces three-dimensional characters and surroundings while retaining the conversations, hidden puzzles and animated storytelling that give the professor's journeys their familiar rhythm.

cards.heading: A gentleman behind a mask
cards.text: Professor Layton and the Miracle Mask is Level-5's puzzle adventure set in Monte d'Or, a city troubled by the apparently supernatural performances of a masked gentleman. Hershel Layton arrives with Luke and Emmy after receiving a request from an old friend. The investigation also returns to his youth, connecting the present mystery with an earlier expedition. Released alongside the Nintendo 3DS in Japan, it introduces three-dimensional characters and surroundings while retaining the conversations, hidden puzzles and animated storytelling that give the professor's journeys their familiar rhythm.

cards.heading: A magnifying glass crosses two screens
cards.text: The touchscreen now moves a magnifying glass across the scene on the upper display. A change in its appearance identifies something worth examining, whether a person, a hidden coin or another part of the location. Players can zoom into selected areas to inspect them more closely. Puzzles still use the touchscreen, with hints available in exchange for collected coins. Solving a puzzle earns Picarats, with mistakes reducing the reward. The revised interface lets the new three-dimensional locations remain visible while the player's hand directs the investigation below.

cards.heading: Layton before the professor
cards.text: Sections following the young Layton place him inside underground ruins, where moving boulders and avoiding mummies turn exploration into a more continuous spatial puzzle. Other activities include arranging a shop's shelves, guiding a toy robot and teaching a rabbit actions for a performance. These smaller systems extend through puzzles found along the main journey. They give the notebook purposes beyond storing clues, while the alternating periods reveal a protagonist who already had friends, doubts and unfinished experiences before becoming the gentleman Luke knows.

main.title: Ridge Racer 3D
main.subtitle: Drifting between two screens
main.summary: Ridge Racer 3D brings the series' high-speed races and drifting to Nintendo 3DS, with a simplified control for beginners and local multiplayer challenges.

cards.heading: Ridge Racer meets the 3D screen
cards.text: Ridge Racer 3D is a 2011 racing video game developed and published by Namco Bandai Games for the Nintendo 3DS. It is the first Ridge Racer series title on a Nintendo platform since Ridge Racer DS (2004) and, as usual for the series, revolves around cars racing around high speed tracks while drifting. The game received positive reviews and was a commercial success. Namco Bandai had announced the creation of a Ridge Racer for Nintendo's upcoming system at E3 2010. The game was designed to take advantage of the device screen's 3D stereo view.

cards.heading: Drifting, winning cars and chasing a time
cards.text: The game introduces a Drift button, specially designed for beginners to the Ridge Racer series, allowing them to drift easily using one button press. In Grand Prix, players compete in a series of races to win new cars and nitrous kits or make them available for purchase. In Time Attack, they race around a track for three laps to achieve the fastest time or beat a ghost.

cards.heading: Races over local wireless
cards.text: The two main gameplay categories are Single Player and Versus. Versus allows players to compete over a Nintendo 3DS local wireless connection by hosting or joining a race. It includes Standard Race, One-Make Race and Team Battle.

cards.heading: Rankings, replays and the garage
cards.text: Records lets players view their Single Player results and local rankings based on records acquired from friends or through StreetPass. AV Player shows replays of past races with music of the player's choice. Options and Garage complete these functions; in the garage, players can view and modify cars they have acquired.

main.title: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy
main.subtitle: Final Fantasy warriors meet before the previous war
main.summary: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy is Square Enix's PSP fighting game, first released in Japan on 3 March 2011. Characters drawn from different Final Fantasy worlds take part in another cycle of the struggle between Cosmos and Chaos. The new campaign precedes the original Dissidia, then includes a revised version of that earlier story. Battles turn familiar heroes and villains into directly controlled fighters, while role-playing development and a world map connect the individual encounters. The release is both an expansion of the original idea and a new route through the crossover's continuing conflict.

cards.heading: Final Fantasy warriors meet before the previous war
cards.text: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy is Square Enix's PSP fighting game, first released in Japan on 3 March 2011. Characters drawn from different Final Fantasy worlds take part in another cycle of the struggle between Cosmos and Chaos. The new campaign precedes the original Dissidia, then includes a revised version of that earlier story. Battles turn familiar heroes and villains into directly controlled fighters, while role-playing development and a world map connect the individual encounters. The release is both an expansion of the original idea and a new route through the crossover's continuing conflict.

cards.heading: An ally can interrupt the decisive attack
cards.text: Assist characters add another resource to the one-on-one battle, allowing support to change a dangerous situation or extend an opportunity. The player has to judge when that intervention is worth using rather than treating it as an automatic addition to every exchange. Familiar fighters and new arrivals bring different abilities into the arenas, encouraging the player to learn another style after mastering a favourite. Movement and attack remain tied to each character's particular strengths, while equipment and development give the wider campaign another layer beyond the immediate result of a duel.

cards.heading: A substantial return to the first Dissidia
cards.text: Mitsunori Takahashi directed and Ichiro Hazama produced, with Takeharu Ishimoto composing the music. Development began in 2009 to refine the earlier systems, adjust their balance and introduce further features. A traditional world map gives the story another structure, while the inclusion of the previous campaign makes the release broader than a short prequel. International editions followed within March 2011. Reviews frequently placed it among the PSP's strongest games, recognising how the expanded cast, revised combat and extensive campaign gave the crossover idea more room to develop.
